author: reek
body: The network authority scope is enforced at RUNTIME, and this is the test that says so -- the twin of scope-runtime-deny for the filesystem path.

author: reek
body: Until now a Network scope literal was a compile-time lint and nothing more: the checker refused an out-of-scope URL it could SEE (keyed on the operation), and any URL the program built from input walked past the promise. Here the scope reaches the wire: the boot grant writes the authority into proc 0's process-table entry, and the fetch chokepoint asks for it before it opens a socket.

author: reek
body: The answer is one number: ten if the in-scope URL is admitted, plus one if the out-of-scope URL is admitted. 10 is the only pass. 11 means the gate is open. 0 or 1 means it denied the host it was told to allow.
